absent: Full definitions, sizes and offsets of machine check record, wrapper, bank and configuration structures.
Severity grading rules and numeric thresholds for keep, recoverable and panic levels.
Auxiliary state capture, logging and firmware interaction side effects.
Register access mechanics and architectural violation conditions beyond panic behavior.
Default values and valid ranges for recovery, timeout, printing and helper configuration.
Complete broadcast exception entry and exit flow outside start, end and reign phases.
Page recovery behavior when advanced memory failure handling is enabled.
Helper path configuration and deferred workqueue processing details.
Synchronization for shared bank control arrays and per processor error records.
Vendor specific memory classification logic for AMD family parts.

findings.text: Exposes a drain operation for pending hardware error events that removes every queued node at once, discards later duplicates and hands back the survivors in reversed order, reporting absence when the queue was empty.
Exposes a queue emptiness test for the pending hardware error list.

Exposes a vendor sensitive predicate that reports whether a machine check record describes memory, delegating AMD family cases externally while applying compound status code pattern checks for Intel family cases and declining other vendors.

Exposes a fault handler for register accesses performed in machine check context that records access direction and register identity with instruction location, emits a stack trace and terminates via panic without returning.
Exposes a register state stack dumper that forwards the current task and supplied register snapshot to the generic trace logger at default verbosity.
Exposes a trigger that schedules deferred helper work only when a helper path is configured, with a companion empty inline variant that performs no action when the feature is unavailable.
Exposes a fallback page recovery routine active without smarter handling that rejects action required requests as a bug, logs the ignored page and reports success.
Entry invoked by the machine check notifier chain at early priority that ignores missing payloads, records a trace entry and requests deferred helper work before reporting completion.

Entry invoked for uncorrected errors that proceeds only with a usable address and an action optional or deferred severity, translating the address to a page frame and marking the record handled when recovery succeeds.
Entry registered at lowest priority to run last that prints records lacking handling marks, or every record when verbose printing is enabled, and always reports completion.
Deferred work entry that checks the pending queue and schedules processing work when entries remain.

Task work orchestration that captures fault address and flags on first user access error, selects among immediate termination, conditional recovery with reexecution barrier, or kernel poison logging paths, and escalates to panic after excessive consecutive faults.
Two records compare different when any of bank identity, status, address or miscellaneous extension differs, forming the duplicate suppression equivalence.
Fallback firmware error reporting uniformly signals invalid argument without side effects.
Whole page determination returns true when software error recovery is disabled or miscellaneous validity is absent, otherwise compares the address significance field against the page size shift.

Error reporting always identifies processor, global status, bank and status registers plus timing and platform topology, conditionally adds instruction location with exactness and symbolic decoding for kernel addresses, address and extension fields when present, and vendor syndrome fields only when extended error extensions are active, while a wrapper adds a decoding hint for non AMD family vendors under rate limiting.
Auxiliary dump returns platform specific memory information only when a confidential memory bug is present on the boot processor, otherwise no information.
Initial broadcast state starts with zeroed sequencing counters and a missing set covering every processor.
Notifier registrations bind early, uncorrected and default handlers with descending priorities ensuring early execution first and default printing last.

Instruction fetch quirk applies only to the lowest bank when global instruction pointer validity is absent and status matches a precise uncorrected enabled signalling action required instruction fetch pattern, in which case it restores instruction pointer validity and address from the trap frame.

Accelerated string quirk proceeds only for local machine checks with string acceleration enabled, and when the second bank shows a software recoverable data fetch pattern it disables acceleration, clears that bank status, logs a one time erratum notice and reports success.
Zen instruction fetch quirk applies only to the second bank when poisoning is indicated, copying the code segment from the trap frame.

Fatal prescan walks all banks on the current processor, collects validated statuses, applies enabled processor specific instruction fetch adjustments, and reports fatal when severity grading reaches panic level after capturing auxiliary state.

Timeout helper diverts to panic wait when another processor already panicked, otherwise when a monarch timeout is configured it reports nonresponsive processors on expiry and panics, decrementing the remaining budget and refreshing the watchdog on each poll.

Crash path filter for offline or non crashing processors dismisses the event and clears global status when restart instruction pointer validity is present, with an additional local exception requirement for one vendor family.
State clearing writes zero to status registers solely for banks flagged in the supplied mask across the current processor bank count.

Fatal handling elects a single panicking processor through atomic increments with distinct accounting for real and synthetic panics, drains pending records printing corrected entries before uncorrected ones with the triggering record last, appends explanatory and auxiliary memory information, poisons the faulting page when crash capture is armed and address validity holds, then panics or emits a synthetic panic notice.

Broadcast rendezvous accumulates each participant arrival and fatal vote, clears the caller from the missing set, waits for full online participation, then assigns order based roles where the first arrival proceeds as coordinator and later arrivals proceed sequentially in arrival order, caching the global fatal flag before returning the order.

Broadcast completion advances a shared execution counter, has the coordinator wait for all participants before grading and resetting global state while subjects wait for the coordinator to finish, and on any timeout or missing configuration resets call in and fatal state and releases waiters.

Coordinator grading examines per processor worst records across all possible processors, panics with refreshed explanation when any fatal severity exists, panics on unknown source when no severity exceeds keep level, otherwise clears all per processor records for the next event.

Per processor bank scanning skips unvalidated or disabled banks and validated but empty statuses, defers corrected or nonsignalled entries unless a fatal condition exists, ignores unhandled severities, otherwise records auxiliary state, logs the event, tracks the worst severity with its copy and counts tainted banks while marking cleared banks.

Observed hardware error record carries bank, status, address, miscellaneous, global status, instruction pointer and segment, timestamp, processor and topology identifiers, microcode, severity and kernel flags, wrapped with vendor syndrome extensions and queue linkage for pending events.

Coordination relies exclusively on atomic counters and a missing processor mask with memory barriers rather than sleeping locks, using single winner panic increments, call in and execution sequencing counters and a global fatal accumulator drained via lock free list removal.

Several paths never return normally: register access faults always panic after tracing, panic wait disables preemption while enabling interrupts during a microsecond scale spin before forcing timeout inheritance and panic, and excessive consecutive user access faults escalate to panic.
Synthetic panic mode suppresses verbose console handling and limits logging to a single reporter, altering observable panic output and avoiding system termination.
Machine check panic peer wait interval is five seconds.
